name: Encoded PowerShell command
description: PowerShell was launched with a Base64-encoded command, a very common obfuscation and execution technique used to hide intent from log review.

name: PowerShell download cradle
description: A remote payload is downloaded and piped straight into execution (download-and-run), a hallmark of staged malware delivery.

name: Invoke-Expression on dynamic input
description: Invoke-Expression runs a string as code. Legitimate but heavily abused to execute obfuscated or remotely fetched scripts.

name: Hidden / execution-policy-bypass PowerShell
description: Flags used to run PowerShell invisibly and without profile/policy restrictions. Common in malicious one-liners; rare in normal interactive use.

name: certutil used as a downloader / decoder
description: certutil is a signed Windows binary abused to download files or decode Base64 payloads, bypassing application controls (a 'living off the land' technique).

name: Signed-binary proxy execution (LOLBin)
description: Trusted Microsoft-signed binaries invoked to proxy-execute remote or scriptlet payloads, evading naive allow-listing.

name: Office application spawned a shell
description: A Microsoft Office process launched a scripting/shell child process, the classic signature of a malicious macro or document lure.

name: Registry Run-key persistence
description: An autorun value is written under a Run/RunOnce key so a program relaunches at logon, a common persistence mechanism.

name: Scheduled-task creation
description: A scheduled task is registered. Legitimate for admin work, but also a frequent persistence and delayed-execution technique.

name: Credential-dumping indicators
description: Strings associated with dumping credentials from LSASS memory (e.g. Mimikatz, comsvcs MiniDump, procdump on lsass).

name: AMSI bypass attempt
description: References to the Antimalware Scan Interface internals, typical of in-memory AMSI bypasses that blind script scanning.

name: Defender tampering
description: Windows Defender real-time protection is being disabled or given exclusions, a common step to blind the endpoint before further activity.

name: Large Base64 blob in command line
description: An unusually long Base64 string embedded in a command line, often an encoded payload or shellcode. Low confidence on its own; corroborate with other signals.

name: Host / domain reconnaissance command
description: Built-in discovery commands attackers run soon after gaining access to map the host and domain. Benign individually; suspicious in bursts.
